findings.title: Tenant external-ID lookups are always empty
findings.failure: Batch imports now collect lookup IDs from `recordsWithTenantStubs`, which is explicitly filtered to records whose `tenantExternalIds` are absent or empty. The resulting map is therefore empty. Customers are imported without tenant memberships, while tenant-centric jobs skip every customer using `tenantExternalIds`. Standalone `importCustomer` callers also receive an empty map fallback, affecting thread, thread-message, and nested-record imports.
findings.fix: Build the batch lookup from `inRecords.flatMap(record => record.tenantExternalIds ?? [])`. When `tenantsByExternalId` is not explicitly supplied to `importCustomer`, retain the old per-customer aggregate lookup. Add coverage for both batch and standalone paths.
findings.evidence: Lines 485-487 exclude records with external IDs, but lines 510-513 read external IDs from that excluded set. The installed `lodash-es/chunk.js` returns `[]` for an empty input, so no aggregate call occurs. Lines 327-331 then resolve no tenants. Repo-wide `rg` found standalone calls without a map in `importAllCustomersAndUsersInRecords.ts:59`, `importThreads.ts:140`, and `importThreadMessage.ts:150`. Salesforce, HubSpot, and Attio customer adapters all populate `tenantExternalIds`.

findings.title: The no-op fast path drops import-job attribution updates
findings.failure: When an existing customer is re-imported under a new import-job definition with no ordinary field changes, the fast path returns `NOOP`. The stored `imported_by_job_definition_id` remains null or stale, and the previous customer-changed event is not emitted.
findings.fix: Pass `importedByJobDefinitionId` as the third argument to `shouldPerformCustomerUpsertUpdate` in the fast path. Add a litest proving that a differing job ID opens a transaction and updates the customer, while an identical ID remains transaction-free.
findings.evidence: The new call at lines 658-660 omits `importedByJobDefinitionId`. The same helper's slow-path call at lines 1026-1033 includes it, and helper tests at `shouldPerformCustomerUpsertUpdate.test.ts:105-116` explicitly establish that a differing job ID is an update even with empty `onUpdate`. `parseImportCustomer` produces `onUpdate: {}`, and `importCustomer` passes the job ID at lines 406-415.

findings.title: Chunk lookup failures are converted into successful partial imports
findings.failure: A permission or database failure for any tenant lookup chunk is logged and ignored. The batch continues with a partial map, causing missing tenant memberships or false tenantless-customer skips while returning a successful import result. The old implementation failed the affected import instead.
findings.fix: Return `Result.err(lookupResult.error)` from `getTenantsByExternalId` and let `importCustomers` abort, preserving the previous failure semantics. Do not log-and-continue a failed Result.
findings.evidence: Lines 282-285 use `continue` after an error, and line 290 always returns `Result.ok`. In HEAD~1, `importCustomer` returned `scope.fail(ctx, lookupResult.error)` for the same aggregate failure at old lines 301-306. This also violates the repository rule that logging and continuing is not sufficient Result handling.

findings.title: The batched lookup Err branch is unreachable
findings.failure: The newly added `tenantsByExternalIdResult.isErr` branch cannot execute because `getTenantsByExternalId` catches every lookup error and has only one return statement: `Result.ok(...)`. It falsely suggests that lookup failures propagate.
findings.fix: Make `getTenantsByExternalId` return `Result.err` on a failed chunk; that makes the existing caller branch meaningful. If failures are intentionally tolerated, return a plain `Map` and remove the dead Result branch instead.
findings.evidence: Repo-wide `rg -n "getTenantsByExternalId"` found only the definition at line 273 and this call at line 510. Inspection of the complete helper shows no Err return path.

checked_fine: Deploy: no infrastructure, migration, environment-variable, permission, secret, export, or provider-state changes are present; the added Lodash imports use an already-consumed dependency.
Contract: routes, methods, schemas, and event versions are unchanged; the new map parameter is optional at the type level.

Data and rollback: no destructive migration, deletion, retention change, or one-way transform was introduced. Reverting restores the old lookup/update behavior, and a later re-import can repair omitted memberships and attribution.

Upsert parity: permission checks, creation behavior, real field updates, email/company resolution, transaction use for writes, and customer-changed event publication remain intact outside the import-job attribution case.
Blast radius: repo-wide caller tracing found no caller outside the importer path that supplies `importedByJobDefinitionId`, so the fast-path regression is scoped to job-driven customer imports.
Operability: no duplicated deployment configuration or missing redeploy trigger was introduced.
Design: aggregate boundaries are preserved, no database module is accessed externally, and no additional refactor is required beyond the fixes above.
